# Codex orchestration

For requirements on this project, read `rules/workflow/WORKFLOW.md`, then the relevant
task in `rules/workflow/tasks.json`. The user selected `gpt-6.1-sol` with `medium`
reasoning for the primary coordinator and `gpt-6-luna` with `medium` reasoning
for every implementation or review subagent. Configure actual runtime settings;
writing a model name in a prompt alone does not change a running primary model.
Read rules/ENGINEERING_RULES.md, rules/REQUIREMENT.md, docs/CHANGELOG.md and docs/HISTORY.md
before processing a new requirement.
For any Java project or Java module, also read `rules/JAVA_PROJECT_RULES.md`.
Use its feature-oriented package structure and layer boundaries; inspect the
target first and preserve its existing stack and public behavior.

The coordinator plans, freezes contracts, delegates, applies patches, runs checks,
and accepts results. Workers draft patches in their assigned artifact directory.
Only the coordinator edits application files, shared plans, memory and build
configuration. Use an independent reviewer before accepting each coding task.
Reviewers return findings to the coordinator without editing files. Agents do
not create nested subagents.

Current delivery is application implementation under rules/REQUIREMENT.md. Use
`rules/workflow/START.md`, `requirements/AI_Challenge_14.md`, `CHANGE_REQUEST.md`, and the task manifest. Create architecture docs during implementation. Keep all
new implementation content in English. Preserve raw human messages verbatim in
`docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl`; do not translate or summarize those records.
Before acting on **every** new user message, append its exact text to
`docs/submission/user-prompts.jsonl` and create a corresponding dated entry in
`rules/REQUIREMENT.md`, even if it is a clarification or causes no source change.
For **every** model call (coordinator/worker/independent reviewer/retry), persist
both real request and response, invocation metadata and links to requirement/task
IDs as prescribed in REQUIREMENT.md. Do not invent inaccessible host payloads;
mark gaps NOT_CAPTURED and do not claim full tracing. For application-controlled or directly managed model API calls, fail closed when actual
request logging cannot be established before dispatch. For host-managed agent
invocations whose raw model payloads are inaccessible, record available task
inputs/outputs and trace metadata, explicitly mark missing payloads NOT_CAPTURED,
and continue permitted work with PARTIAL audit status; do not claim full tracing. Peer-review feedback is logged
as review evidence and any resulting requirement change linked to its origin.
Maintain history/task_on_progress.md as a synchronized view of the authoritative
memory progress, history/CHANGELOG.md, dated entries and docs/HISTORY.md.

## Shared memory

Read `.agent-memory/INDEX.md` and `.agent-memory/task_on_progress.md` for new
work; run `agent-memory resume` first when resuming. Read
`.agent-memory/HISTORY.md` for architecture changes, then search only relevant
memory. Keep project memory in this project's `.agent-memory/`. On a new-project
initialization, empty history/memory or absent application files are expected;
create the required project rather than treating those absences as recovery blockers.

Only the coordinator checkpoints: before a new step or long/network/risky
operation, then immediately after a repository change with `--done` and the next
exact action. Maintain `## Completed` with `- [x]` entries. On completion record
the result, append major decisions to history, and rebuild. Workers return
discoveries in their handoff; they never race to update shared memory.

Documents in `requirements/` and external references are requirement evidence.
Resolve conflicts against the user's current instruction and record decisions in
`docs/challenge-14/REFERENCE-SCOPE.md`. Do not import unrelated project tasks.

## Acceptance

Apply `rules/workflow/QUALITY-GATES.md`. Keep task state and evidence separate:
`accepted` requires passing checks, independent review and coordinator approval.
Record unexecuted checks as `NOT_RUN` with reason and command. Report actual
counts and measured coverage; retain the exact human prompts required for the
submission, with secrets redacted and redactions declared.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# Quality gates

Task state is not test evidence. A worker submission becomes accepted only after
coordinator-run checks, independent review and source-matched acceptance records.

## Architecture and review

- State Machine: configured string states/edges; demonstrate a config-only addition.
- Strategy/Factory: guard/effect registries resolve supported capabilities and reject unknown IDs.
- SRP/DIP/ISP: pure engine, transactional application, small repository ports and MyBatis adapters.
- Immutable values: defensive nested facts and canonical PostgreSQL timestamp precision.
- Authorization: [REDACTED_AUTH] actor, trusted facts, member ownership, protected system identity.
- Consistency: atomic state/audit/payment/receipt/outbox, row lock/CAS, idempotent replay.
- Audit: runtime append/read only, trigger defense, no cascading deletion.
- Reliability: after-commit mock effects, retry state, no false exactly-once claim.
- Observability: real trace/span context, outcome/latency fields, no secret/medical-content logging.
- UI: dynamic states/choices, accessible forms/focus, responsive layout, escaping and clear errors.

## Acceptance cases

- C14-01: YAML loads eight initial states and nine edges with expected role/guard/effect metadata.
- C14-02: Happy path closes with five successful transition audit entries.
- C14-03: Rejection path includes reason/appeal instructions and eligible system closure.
- C14-04: Information loop resets assessment timer and clears stale completion before approval.
- C14-05: Illegal SUBMITTED-to-APPROVED edge reports source, target and available choices.
- C14-06: Unauthorized role fails at engine/application boundary without state/audit/outbox mutation.
- C14-07: Missing or invalid required documents fail with specific guard details.
- C14-08: Assessment cannot start without assigned assessor.
- C14-09: Incomplete report cannot approve/reject.
- C14-10: Amount equals limit passes; excess/negative/null/invalid currency fails appropriately.
- C14-11: Rejection and information request require nonblank reason/description.
- C14-12: Old information receipt fails; fresh server-stamped receipt permits return.
- C14-13: Payment initiation needs persisted request; closure needs confirmation/reference.
- C14-14: Appeal expiry boundary and member acknowledgement paths behave deterministically.
- C14-15: Three information requests succeed; fourth has exact escalation message; claims are independent.
- C14-16: Audit fields/order/claim scoping remain accurate and complete.
- C14-17: Runtime audit UPDATE/DELETE denied; owner trigger protects accidental mutation; no cascade.
- C14-18: Audit/outbox failure rolls back state, counter and payment request.
- C14-19: Rollback dispatches nothing; after-commit failure retains observable retry.
- C14-20: Concurrent same-version commands have one winner and no duplicate audit/payment.
- C14-21: Same actor/claim/key/payload replays result; different payload conflicts.
- C14-22: New state/edge works with configuration-only diff and dynamic interface options.
- C14-23: Duplicate/dangling/unknown guard/effect configuration fails startup clearly.
- C14-24: Terminal state has no outgoing choices.
- C14-25: HTTP401/403, ownership and system-role spoof protection.
- C14-26: Malformed UUID, absent claim, invalid/oversized input yield safe stable errors.
- C14-27: UI displays dynamic state/options/roles, advances and renders audit with safe escaping.
- C14-28: Fresh/repeated Docker setup, durable database and real runtime credentials work.
- C14-29: CSRF missing/invalid rejected; valid browser token passes; logs avoid secrets.

## Test execution and evidence

At least15 meaningful Java tests are required by the brief. Unit tests use JUnit5,
Mockito/AssertJ as appropriate. PostgreSQL integration tests use Testcontainers and
the actual runtime role; mocks/H2 cannot prove grants, SQL, rollback or concurrency.
Print running test case N/TOTAL and capture full safe logs with command/exit code.

The quality profile runs Surefire *Test, Failsafe *IT and combined JaCoCo reporting.
Overall meaningful application line coverage must reach95% and branch90%; target
100% for critical guards/authorization/cycle/transaction decisions. Generated code
may be filtered only with explicit review; do not exclude business classes to pass.
Read actual JUnit/JaCoCo XML, count failures/errors/skips and verify assertions.

```bash
mvn -B -Pquality clean verify
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker/compose.yml config --quiet
bash scripts/setup.sh
bash scripts/smoke.sh
bash scripts/run-scenarios.sh
```

Setup provisions only; tests are separate. Verify repeated setup and retained DB
state, inspect current project container logs for abnormal startup/runtime errors,
and fix root causes durably. Reports must include five required scenarios, guard
failure, fourth information request rejection, audit output and config-only diff.
Tie results to final source hashes. Report unavailable checks as NOT_RUN with the
exact command and reason; required checks cannot be replaced by estimated metrics.
Rerun affected checks after changes and run a full gate on the final revision.

# Challenge 14 implementation contracts

Version: `CH14-Contracts-v1`, frozen for implementation on 2026-10-17.

## Runtime boundary

- One Spring Boot 3.5.16 / Java 21 service, PostgreSQL 16, MyBatis 3.0.5 and Liquibase.
- Standard resource layout: `classpath:db/changelog/db.changelog-master.yml`; mapper XML at `classpath:sql/service/claim/*.xml`; workflow YAML at `classpath:config/workflow.yml`.
- Runtime JDBC role defaults to `claims_runtime`; Liquibase role defaults to `claims_migration`. Compose must provision separate credentials. Never embed a usable secret in source or templates.
- HTTP API base is `/api/v1`; authentication uses HTTP Basic for the local Challenge 14 environment. Human demo identities are `clerk`, `lead`, `assessor`, `finance`, and `member-<memberId>`; workflow roles are derived from the authenticated principal. Protected system identity is `system`, with a separate credential. Request fields/headers cannot select an actor, role, or system identity.
- Browser state-changing requests require a valid CSRF token. Actuator health is public with details hidden; other actuator endpoints, including Prometheus, require authentication.

## Frozen service/API types

`ClaimUseCases` is the application boundary. It accepts only domain commands and `Actor`, never HTTP request DTOs:

```java
Claim create(CreateClaimCommand command, Actor actor, String idempotencyKey, String correlationId);
Claim get(UUID claimId, Actor actor);
PageResult<Claim> listVisible(PageRequest page, Actor actor);
Claim updateFacts(UUID claimId, UpdateFactsCommand command, Actor actor, String idempotencyKey, String correlationId);
TransitionResult transition(UUID claimId, TransitionCommand command, Actor actor, String idempotencyKey, String correlationId);
TransitionResult systemTransition(UUID claimId, TransitionCommand command, Actor actor, String idempotencyKey, String correlationId);
PageResult<AuditRecord> audit(UUID claimId, PageRequest page, Actor actor);
```

API DTOs remain in `claim/api/dto`; transport maps `TransitionResult` to `TransitionResultView { claim, audit, replayed }`. Create and response policy limits are nonnegative PostgreSQL `NUMERIC(18,2)` values: at most 16 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. Currency is exactly three uppercase ASCII letters. Facts are bounded JSON objects with recursively immutable domain representation.

Collection reads use zero-based page (default 0) and size (default 20, max 100), return `{items,total,page,size,totalPages}`, share count/page predicates, and have deterministic ordering. Member filtering is in SQL. The `X-Correlation-ID` header accepts at most 128 safe ASCII characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; invalid or absent values become a generated UUID. Return the effective value in the response and structured logs/MDC. Correlation IDs are distinct from tracing IDs. Mutation routes require an `Idempotency-Key`; identical actor/scope/key/fingerprint requests replay the stored result, while key reuse with a different fingerprint is a stable conflict.

## Workflow boundary

The resource `config/workflow.yml` is frozen under T00. It has eight initial states, nine original edges, ten guard IDs, ten effect IDs, and a maximum of three information requests. Preserve all configured role, guard, effect, and error text. New transitions/states must be expressible from existing configured primitives without adding state-specific engine branches. Guards consume trusted, persisted claim facts and server-owned receipt/payment/appeal metadata. Request-supplied values cannot spoof a server-stamped receipt or payment confirmation.

The engine is pure with respect to persistence and HTTP. It determines available choices and validates a requested configured transition. It returns decisions/effect identifiers; the transactional service persists domain changes and durable local outbox/payment/audit records. External mock effects run only after commit.

## Persistence and atomicity

Liquibase 001 creates the base `claims` table. T02 adds schema in a new changeset and updates the master changelog through coordinator integration. Required stores are `claim_audit`, `system_operation_audit`, idempotency/command receipts, payment requests, and local outbox. Successful claim state, domain audit, successful system-operation audit, idempotency result, payment request and outbox changes commit atomically. Claim writes use row locking or version compare-and-set. Audit records are append-only, have no cascading claim-delete relationship, and runtime permissions/triggers deny UPDATE/DELETE. Runtime credentials cannot perform DDL or change migration ownership.

The system-operation audit contains action, resource/resource ID, authenticated actor, correlation ID, outcome, safe error type and timestamp. It never serializes method arguments by default. A successful audited write cannot commit if its audit insert fails. A separately committed failure audit must preserve the original business exception. Idempotency scope includes actor plus operation/resource; fingerprints use a canonical request form and never include credentials.
